method: Text color = computed CSS color of the element. Background = average of a ~8-10x10 pixel grid sampled from a full-page screenshot within the element's bounding rect. Because glyphs are thin relative to their box, this approximates the background BEHIND the text but is pulled slightly toward the glyph color itself (a conservative bias -- true bg-only contrast is usually >= reported here). bgLumSpread reports max-min luminance in the sampled grid: near 0 means a flat/uniform sampled region (little text detected in-box or a very flat background). All text-shadow is force-disabled (* { text-shadow: none !important }) before every sample so glow halos are never measured as background. Elements with no visible text content (empty label-less boxes, e.g. locked fog-of-war key boxes) are skipped entirely rather than reported.

thresholds.pass: >= 4.5 (WCAG AA large-text min is 3:1; this project targets higher for a 5-year-old reader)
